title: Size-tunable and surface-functionalized hydrophilic magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles prepared by one-pot synthesis
content: Despite the clinical success of iron oxide (Fe3O4) nanoparticles in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), those prepared by conventional coprecipitation methods often exhibit relatively broad particle size distributions and limited crystallinity, constraining their broader clinical applicability. We previously reported a one-step thermal decomposition method using iron(iii) acetylacetonate and a methoxy-PEG2K-maleimide (mPEG2K-Mal) ligand to directly produce water-dispersible and maleimide-functionalized Fe3O4 (Fe3O4-Mal) nanoparticles with narrow size distributions. Here, by regulating the heating rate and PEG terminal groups, we further broadened the accessible size range of Fe3O4-Mal nanoparticles to approximately 10–21 nm. Among these, the larger 21 nm Fe3O4-Mal nanoparticles prepared by substituting the methoxy PEG terminus with a carboxyl group demonstrated high biomolecule conjugation capacity while maintaining good colloidal stability and biocompatibility. Furthermore, the modular PEG-based strategy can be extended to other conjugation handles by substituting the maleimide group. This work expands the one-pot PEG-mediated synthesis strategy to enable tunable particle size and surface functionality, offering the potential to address key limitations associated with clinically approved Fe3O4 nanoparticles and facilitate the development of magnetic nanocarriers for diverse biomedical and clinical applications.
